summary.title: OpenCV OCR and text recognition with Tesseract
summary.one_liner: You learn to build an OpenCV OCR pipeline in Python that detects text regions with the EAST detector and then recognizes them with Tesseract 4's LSTM engine.
keywords: how do i read text from an image with opencv
takeaways: Tesseract 4 includes an LSTM-based deep learning OCR engine, selected with --oem 1.
OpenCV's EAST detector finds text bounding boxes, which are then cropped and passed to Tesseract via pytesseract.
The --psm flag (for example 7 for a single line, or 6 for a block) strongly affects OCR accuracy and should be tuned.
Installation steps differ by platform: apt on Ubuntu 18.04, Homebrew on macOS, and a community build on Raspberry Pi.
summary.summary: The tutorial shows how to combine OpenCV's EAST text detector with Tesseract v4 to perform OCR on natural scene images. It covers installing Tesseract 4 and pytesseract on Ubuntu, macOS, and Raspberry Pi, then explains the key Tesseract flags (-l, --oem, --psm). The main part walks through a text_recognition.py script line by line: decoding EAST predictions, applying non-maxima suppression, scaling and padding boxes, and running pytesseract on each region of interest. A July 2021 update adds a section on alternatives such as cloud OCR engines and EasyOCR.
